configurePresets.name: base
configurePresets.description: FFmpeg is on here rather than left to the option default, which is OFF. Without it a fresh clone silently builds no AAC, ALAC, WMA, AC3, DTS or TAK, and CI never compiles that decoder at all. The option stays OFF by default for anyone configuring by hand who does not want the dependency. Crash reporting is on for the same reason and with the same caveat: the reporter is built, and stays inert until the listener consents to it.

configurePresets.name: app-only
configurePresets.description: Just the application: no xpcog-cli, no test suite. What this saves is compile and link time only -- vcpkg still installs the catch2 default feature, because features cannot be subtracted from an inherited list without restating the whole of it (see linux-headless), and unlike the sentry case that taught that lesson, catch2 costs a download rather than a crashpad build. Each concrete preset below configures its own build tree named after itself, as every preset here does.

configurePresets.name: linux
configurePresets.description: Restates VCPKG_MANIFEST_FEATURES without `gui`, which is how the toolkit is left to the distribution here. vcpkg's wxwidgets port depends on its gtk3 port, so asking vcpkg for wx on Linux builds GTK and about thirty packages under it -- glib, pango, cairo, harfbuzz, fontconfig, at-spi2, dbus, seven X11 libraries -- from source, on a machine that already has every one of them. Install libwxgtk3.2-dev instead; cmake/XPCogWx.cmake finds it. A feature cannot be subtracted from an inherited list, hence the restatement rather than an override, the same way macos-headless does it. `sentry` stays: it is the toolkit that comes from the distribution here, not the crash reporter.

configurePresets.name: linux-repo
configurePresets.description: The Linux build, taking every dependency the distribution already has at a version this code can use, and asking vcpkg only for the rest. Same source, same options and the same feature list as `linux` -- the one cache variable below is what makes cmake/XPCogSystemDeps.cmake probe with pkg-config before project() and subtract what it finds from VCPKG_MANIFEST_FEATURES. On a developer machine with the -dev packages installed that is most of the manifest, FFmpeg and OpenSSL included, which is nearly all of a cold build. The plain linux-debug and linux-release presets stay as they were and take everything from vcpkg: that is what CI builds, and what a build has to be to be reproducible on a machine other than the one it was configured on.

configurePresets.name: linux-headless
configurePresets.displayName: Linux headless (core + cli + tests, no toolkit)
configurePresets.description: What CI's headless Linux job builds. It used to say `--preset linux-debug -D XPCOG_BUILD_APP=OFF`, which stopped being enough when the crash reporter arrived: XPCOG_BUILD_APP=OFF means platform/ is never added and nothing links sentry, but vcpkg decides what to install from the feature list and installed it anyway -- so the job built crashpad, and libunwind under it, for a target that could not use either. Features cannot be subtracted from an inherited list, so `sentry` is dropped by restating, the same way macos-headless drops `gui`. The list lives here rather than in a -D on the CI step for the reason the comment on that step gives: one list, in one file.

configurePresets.name: macos-headless
configurePresets.displayName: macOS headless (core + cli + tests, no Qt)
configurePresets.description: Restates VCPKG_MANIFEST_FEATURES without `gui` because it inherits the list and a feature cannot be subtracted. Building wx here would cost a GTK build for a target that links no toolkit. `sentry` goes too, and for the matching reason: XPCOG_BUILD_APP is off, so the platform layer that holds the crash reporter is never added, and building crashpad for it would be a helper executable with nothing to sit beside.
